raw_answer_text:
A1: The unicast routing table (routing information base).
A2: The packet's source address.
A3: It tells the router the next-hop (upstream) neighbor, in addition to the outgoing interface toward that source.
A4: It compares that interface against the interface on which the packet actually arrived.
A5: The router first looks up the route back toward the source, then compares it to the arrival interface.
A6: It passes when the arrival interface matches the interface that routing indicates is used to reach the source; the router accepts/forwards the packet (e.g., onto the multicast tree).
A7: It fails when the arrival interface does not match the expected interface toward the source; the router drops the packet.
A8: It's "reverse" because it checks the path back toward where the packet came from (the source), rather than the normal forwarding path toward the destination.
